Technology stocks were posting strong gains Monday afternoon, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 adding almost 0.8% while the Philadelphia semiconductor index was posting a more than 1.0% advance.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ Ceragon Networks ( CRNT ) rose Monday, topping out with an 8% advance, after the networking equipment manufacturer reported adjusted Q1 earnings and revenue beating Wall Street estimates. Excluding one-time items, it earned $0.04 per share, improving a penny over its year-ago non-GAAP profit and exceeding the two-analyst consensus by $0.01 per share. Revenue climbed 9.5% year over year to $83.3 million during the January-to-March fiscal period, also surpassing the $79.8 million Street view.
In other sector news:
+ Welbilt ( WBT ) rose Monday after the company reported adjusted Q1 net income of $0.15 per share, up from $0.08 last year during the same quarter last year and beating the Capital IQ consensus by $0.04 per share. Revenue during the three months ended March 31 grew to $350.4 million from $328.0 million last year, also exceeding the $329.9 million analyst mean. The company also is projecting adjusted FY18 net income in a range of $0.80 to $0.90 per share and net sales growth of between 7% to 10% over FY17 sales. Analysts, on average, are modeling for non-GAAP FY18 EPS of $0.88 on 7.7% year-over-year sales growth to around 1.56 billion.
- TowerJazz ( TSEM ) tumbled Monday, at one point falling as much as 20%, after the company reported weaker-than-expected Q1 results. Excluding one-time items, the company earned $0.31 per share during the three months ended March 31, down from $0.49 per share during the year-ago period and trailing the Capital IQ consensus by $0.10 per share. Revenue dropped to to $312.7 million from $330.1 million last year, also coming in below the $325 million analyst mean.
